questions.title: Aircraft in horizontal circle — centripetal acceleration & banking angle

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The acceleration is (always) perpendicular to the velocity, directed towards the centre of the circle, and the magnitudes of the velocity (the speed) and of the acceleration are constant — but their directions change continuously.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The only other force on the aircraft is its weight, which is vertical and has no horizontal component. The lift must therefore have a horizontal component (the resultant force towards the centre of the circle) to provide the centripetal force — so the lift cannot be vertically upwards.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Arrow drawn from the aircraft pointing horizontally to the left, i.e. towards the centre of the circle — the resultant force provides the centripetal force.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
The vertical component of the lift balances the weight (L cos θ = mg) and the horizontal component of the lift causes the centripetal acceleration (L sin θ = ma):
tan θ = a/g = 4.5/9.81
θ = 25°

questions.title: Earth's gravitational field — mass, potential & satellite energy

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The gravitational field (strength) at a point is the force per unit mass acting on a small test mass placed at that point.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw four straight, parallel field lines perpendicular to the ground (vertical), approximately evenly spaced, with arrows pointing downwards towards the ground.

questions.title: Cooling gas at constant pressure — internal energy & specific heat capacity

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the thermal energy per unit mass per unit change in temperature.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The volume of the gas decreases (the gas is compressed), so the work done on the gas is positive.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
For an ideal gas the internal energy is proportional to the thermodynamic temperature (U = ³⁄₂NkT). At constant pressure the temperature is proportional to the volume, so the internal energy falls to 80% of its initial value:
ΔU = −0.20×3676 = −735 J

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
First law: ΔU = Q + W (W is the work done on the gas)
−735 = Q + 491
Q = −1226 J (thermal energy is removed from the gas)

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The same temperature change gives the same change in internal energy as in (b). At constant volume no work is done on or by the gas (W = 0), so from ΔU = Q + W only 735 J of thermal energy needs to be supplied — less than the 1226 J removed in (b). Hence c = Q/(mΔT) is less than the value in (b)(v).

questions.title: Particle in a cubic box — momentum change & pressure derivation

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Any two of: collisions between particles and with the walls are instantaneous (collision time negligible compared with the time between collisions); collisions are perfectly elastic (no kinetic energy is lost).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
The momentum reverses from +mu to −mu:
change in momentum = 2mu

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The particle travels a distance 2L (there and back) between successive collisions with the same face:
time = 2L/u

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
F = Δp/t = 2mu/(2L/u)
= mu²/L

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
By Newton's third law the force exerted on the face by the particle is equal (and opposite) to the force exerted on the particle by the face. Pressure = force/area:
p = F/A = (mu²/L)/L² = mu²/L³

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
Three modifications: the volume of the cube L³ is the volume V of the gas, so pV = mu²; particles move in three (all) dimensions, so only one-third of the mean-square speed acts along any one axis — u² becomes ⅓⟨c²⟩; with N particles the pressure is N times that due to a single particle:
pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩

questions.title: Block oscillating on a spring — amplitude & kinetic energy

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: The amplitude is the magnitude of the maximum displacement of the block from its equilibrium (mean) position.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Sketch a dome-shaped curve, symmetrical about the EK-axis, with a single peak of 13 μJ at x = 0, falling to EK = 0 at x = ±8.4×10⁻³ m (the amplitude). Add a consistent x-axis scale with at least one marking in each half (e.g. ±8 and ±4, in units of 10⁻³ m), corresponding to the end points.

questions.title: Charged conducting sphere — electric potential & dome capacitance

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The electric potential at a point is the work done per unit positive charge in bringing a small test charge from infinity to the point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: V₀ = Q/(4πε₀R), where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Sketch a curve starting at (R, V₀) that falls with decreasing magnitude of V and of gradient (V = Q/4πε₀x), passing through (2R, ½V₀) and (3R, ⅓V₀), entirely within the positive V region and approaching the x-axis without crossing it.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: The dome stores charge (and hence energy) at a potential — it can be charged and discharged — so it acts as a capacitor: its capacitance is the charge stored per unit p.d.

questions.title: Hall probe in a magnetic field — Hall voltage & charge carriers

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The Hall voltage is induced between faces PSZW and QRYX.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
n = number density of charge carriers (number per unit volume);
q = charge on each charge carrier;
t = thickness of the slice (the distance between faces PSZW and QRYX).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Any three of: the charge carriers experience a force due to the magnetic field; the force on the carriers is perpendicular to both I and B; the carriers deflect towards one face (accumulating there, leaving the opposite face with the opposite charge); the charge separation between the faces produces a p.d. (the Hall voltage) between them; a steady state is reached when the magnetic force is balanced by the force due to the resulting electric field.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The (negative) electrons are deflected towards face QRYX, leaving face PSZW positively charged — face PSZW is at the higher potential.

questions.title: Rectification & smoothing of a sinusoidal input voltage

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Diode (single diode producing half-wave rectification).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Capacitor (connected in parallel across the output).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: peak value of VIN = 3.6 V

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: period of VIN = 0.040 s

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Any three of: the rectification is half-wave (VOUT is zero during alternate half-cycles); frequency of VIN = 1/0.040 = 25 Hz (angular frequency 160 rad s⁻¹); r.m.s. input voltage = 3.6/√2 = 2.5 V; time constant of the smoothing circuit = 0.058 s; ripple (variation in VOUT) = 1.6 V (44% of the peak).

questions.title: Electron accelerated by 3.5 kV — speed & de Broglie wavelength

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The de Broglie wavelength is the wavelength associated with a moving particle (λ = h/p).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Wave nature of matter: electron diffraction (or electron interference);
particle nature of matter: states of matter / state changes / gas behaviour / quantisation of charge / radioactive decay / Rutherford scattering / Brownian motion;
wave nature of EM radiation: diffraction / interference / polarisation;
particle nature of EM radiation: photoelectric effect (or emission/absorption line spectra, Compton scattering).

questions.title: Star fusing hydrogen to helium — binding energy & mass loss

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The binding energy of a nucleus is the energy required to separate all the nucleons (protons and neutrons) in the nucleus to infinity — equivalently, the energy released when the nucleons come together to form the nucleus.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: 4 ¹H → ⁴He + 2X, so X is the positron (β⁺).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Number of He-4 nuclei formed per second = L/E_He = 7.98×10²⁷/4.54×10⁻¹² = 1.76×10³⁹ s⁻¹. Each He-4 nucleus is formed from 4 hydrogen nuclei, each of mass 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg:
mass rate = 4×1.67×10⁻²⁷×7.98×10²⁷/4.54×10⁻¹²
= 1.17×10¹³ kg s⁻¹
